frequency_question: How often does the central bank deploy an incremental cash reserve ratio or equivalent targeted liquidity impounding mechanism during periods of sudden banking system surplus within a defined four-month window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal RBI circular or press release mandating banks to maintain incremental cash balances on a specified base of deposits. Excludes standard CRR changes, regular variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auctions, and standard OMOs.
window: Any four-month calendar period between 2006 and 2026.
provenance_note: 3 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 3 named key episodes; estimated 6 total major liquidity surplus surge episodes requiring extraordinary ratio tools in 20 years.
known_gaps: Minor ad-hoc circulars addressing isolated bank-level liquidity may be omitted if not system-wide.
skeleton: RBI policy cycles over 20 years examined for discrete liquidity shocks requiring targeted ratio adjustments rather than rate adjustments.
multiplier: 2 hits out of roughly 6 distinct unexpected surplus shock windows of comparable magnitude yields a baseline frequency.
validity_reason: Central bank operating frameworks for liquidity management evolve slowly over structural policy regimes.
